clue.text: Brief extract from impressive unfinished book

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for impressive loses its final letter

parts.note: something impressive on a grand scale is epic
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A short quotation lifted from a grand book that was never completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like part of the wordplay, shortening something, but it belongs to the definition; 'unfinished' is the cut.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a summary or abridgement, a short condensed version of a longer work.

clue.text: Newcomer's music upset audience finally leaving concert hall, say

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the music's word is turned upside down

parts.note: rap is a kind of music

indicators.note: leaving means a letter departs from the hall's word

parts.note: a concert hall is an example of a venue

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of audience

explanation.surface: A newcomer's song upsets the crowd, which ends up leaving the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RAP into PAR; 'audience finally leaving' takes the E off VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart, someone newly risen to wealth or status.

clue.text: Source of thread in suit woven for someone from central Africa?

indicators.note: source of means the opening letter of thread
woven means the letters are interlaced into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A thread starting point in a woven suit made for an African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges only SUIT; the thread's first letter stands in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi; the question mark notes one example of a central African.

clue.text: Champion footballer visiting a hospital

parts.note: Lionel Messi is an Argentine footballer

explanation.surface: A star footballer calls in at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A messiah is a saviour or liberator, a champion of a cause.

clue.text: Find fault with round metal tool

indicators.note: round here means the metal's word is turned back to front

parts.note: tin is a metal
a pick is a digging tool

explanation.surface: Criticising a circular metal implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as describing the tool's shape, but it signals the turnaround of the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to criticise petty details, finding small faults with something.

clue.text: Points in short typeface set up ready for use

indicators.note: in means the points are placed inside the typeface's word

parts.note: ital is the short form of italic, a typeface
N and S are points of the compass, north and south

explanation.surface: Dots in a reduced font arranged so it can be used.
explanation.definitionFit: To instal, a variant of install, is to put equipment in place ready to work.

clue.text: Puncture found after rope breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of after rope are shattered and recombined

explanation.surface: A hole discovered once a rope snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce holes through something.

clue.text: Eccentric person eating only skimmed milk-based sauce

indicators.note: eating means the eccentric swallows the other piece

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or comical person

indicators.note: skimmed means the top letter is taken off the word for only

parts.note: just means only

explanation.surface: An oddball consuming nothing but a sauce from skimmed milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skimmed' seems to describe the milk, but it takes the top off the word for 'only'; 'eating' does the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce made from milk and eggs.

clue.text: Sly dog dangled bananas for insect

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A crafty dog dangles some bananas to tempt a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly, with its very long thin legs, is commonly called this in Britain.

clue.text: Motif retraced around part of stringed instrument

indicators.note: around here says the letters lie in the words, sitting about the join of Motif and retraced

explanation.surface: A musical motif traced again round some piece of a guitar or violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraced' tempts a backwards reading, but the letters run forwards across 'Motif retraced'.
explanation.definitionFit: Frets are the raised ridges across the neck of a guitar or similar instrument.

clue.text: Master's translated letter for hands-on worker

indicators.note: translated means the letters of Master's are converted into a new form

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A boss's letter, rendered into another language, intended for a manual labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges MASTERS to SEAMSTR; ESS completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressmaker sewing by hand is literally a worker whose hands are on the fabric.

clue.text: Soldier carrying artist's sign

indicators.note: carrying means the soldier's letters hold the artist inside them

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: A soldier holding up a painter's placard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Old Ottoman guide, a bore, going to a sultanate in Arabia

indicators.note: going to means the second piece is joined on after the first

parts.note: a drag is something tedious, a bore
Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A tedious old Turkish guide travelling to an Arabian sultanate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter and guide in Turkish- and Arabic-speaking lands of the Ottoman era.

clue.text: Spooner's other half meeting old king in confined space

indicators.note: Spooner's tells us to swap the opening sounds of the two words, after Rev. William Spooner

parts.note: a spouse, one's other half, is a hubby when a husband
Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: A wife's husband joining a monarch of old in a cramped spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the H of HUBBY and the C of COLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubbyhole is a small snug cupboard or room, a cramped enclosed nook.

clue.text: Cricketer initially happy about the headgear

parts.note: a bowler is a cricketer who delivers the ball

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of happy

parts.note: at can mean about, as in busy at a task

explanation.surface: A cricketer starts out pleased with the cap he has.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the bowler is the player who delivers the ball to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler hat is a hard round felt hat, a piece of headwear.

clue.text: Carry clubs in small container

definitions.meaning: to carry a golfer's bag of clubs is to act as caddie
a small box for keeping tea

explanation.surface: Golf clubs carried inside a little box.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is a golf assistant's job; the noun is a little tin or box for tea leaves.

clue.text: Overweight women given a death sentence

parts.note: overweight means fat

explanation.surface: Heavy women handed capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' of 'a death sentence' gives the last letter, leaving 'death sentence' to define.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is an Islamic legal ruling, notoriously one decreeing that someone be killed.

clue.text: Touching stove isn't funny!

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of range cooker

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of isn't are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone warns that touching the cooker is no joke.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy cast-iron range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning against something means being in contact with it, touching it.

clue.text: Pain relief for north American with broken leg detained in the Far East

indicators.note: detained in means these pieces are held inside the region's name

parts.note: Asia stands for the Far East

indicators.note: broken means the letters of leg are rearranged

explanation.surface: Painkillers for a northern American who broke a leg while held captive in East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles leg; 'detained in' splits ASIA after its first letter to take the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the absence or relief of pain, as given by painkilling drugs.

clue.text: Country where bell sounds rise before long

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the heard word is read upwards
sounds means take what is heard, a word pronounced like bell

parts.note: the word bell is said aloud
anon means soon, before long

explanation.surface: A nation where church bells ring out ahead of a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds' gives the bel, a unit of loudness pronounced like 'bell'; 'rise' turns it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a Middle Eastern country on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Popular copper to transport unwelcome nocturnal visitor

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A well-liked policeman ferrying an unwanted night-time caller.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a demon believed to visit and lie upon sleepers at night.

clue.text: Dump serving as nest for tiny bird ascending

indicators.note: ascending in a down clue means the whole is read upwards
serving as nest for means the dump holds the other word within it

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
wee means tiny

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip is home to a little bird flying upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving as nest for' gives TIWEEP; 'ascending' turns it all upwards, though 'bird' sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is the lapwing, a plover named for its call.

clue.text: Food fit for leave-taking?

parts.note: fare is food served
fit and well both mean healthy

explanation.surface: Is there food suited to a departure?
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a goodbye, the act of parting or departing.

clue.text: Soup recipe secured by painter

indicators.note: secured by means the recipe's letter is held within the painter

parts.note: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter
R is an abbreviation for recipe, from Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A soup recipe kept safe by an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Borsch, also spelt borscht, is an East European beetroot soup.

clue.text: Insurgent put base of bomb in rock

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for rock

parts.note: to reel is to sway or rock

indicators.note: base of in a down clue means the bottom letter of bomb

explanation.surface: A guerrilla places the bottom of an explosive within a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is an insurgent, someone who rises against authority.

clue.text: TT (travelling by truck?)

definitions.meaning: TT stands for teetotal, abstaining from drink
riding a wagon, literally aboard a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A short note glossing teetotal as riding in a lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means abstaining from alcohol; literally it describes riding on a wagon, a truck.

clue.text: Infant born before sailor gets by in the end

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: in the end means only the last letter of by is used

explanation.surface: A child born ahead of a seaman who eventually manages.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an infant, a very young child.

clue.text: Condition endlessly applied to limits of the law

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for condition loses its final letter

parts.note: status is condition or standing

indicators.note: limits of means the outer letters of the word the

explanation.surface: A requirement imposed without end on what the law allows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STATUS to STATU; 'limits of the' gives TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Shingle broken up for old printing type

indicators.note: broken up means the letters of Shingle are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Beach pebbles smashed to bits make an antique typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: English was an old printers' size of type, about 14 point, also a black-letter style.
